Third-party software in the WordPlus SDK's pickers: pickers.min.js, and the emoji datasets in data/emoji/

- emoji-mart 5.6.0 (MIT), Missive: its picker, ported to React and changed (pickers/src/emoji-mart), in pickers.min.js
- @emoji-mart/data (MIT), Missive: the emoji datasets data/emoji/apple.json, google.json, twitter.json and facebook.json
- emoji-datasource (MIT), Cal Henderson: the emoji, their names and their places in the image sheets, which the datasets carry
- react-icons (MIT), kamijin_fanta: the components of three icons, VscClose, VscHistory and VscSearch, in pickers.min.js
- Codicons (CC BY 4.0), Microsoft Corporation: those three icons, the close, history and search icons

pickers/src/emoji-mart/helpers/native-support.ts is based on is-emoji-supported
(https://github.com/koala-interactive/is-emoji-supported, MIT), as emoji-mart's own is.

The emoji images are not in the SDK: browsers load them from the emoji-datasource-<set> packages on jsDelivr, or a
site downloads them there on an administrator's request.

================================================================================
Codicons (CC BY 4.0)
================================================================================

The close, history and search icons of pickers/src/icons.tsx are Codicons, the icons of Visual Studio Code,
by Microsoft Corporation: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-codicons

Copyright (c) Microsoft Corporation.

They are licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International Public License (CC BY 4.0):
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/legalcode

They are used as react-icons publishes them (VscClose, VscHistory and VscSearch), their paths unchanged, drawn as
React components. They are provided as is, without warranties of any kind, as Section 5 of that licence says.
